chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who hired a ship from a sailor, so he loaded it with foodstuff, and he stipulated upon him that if the foodstuff was deficient, it would be upon him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is allowed.' I said to him (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes the foodstuff is excessive.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Does the sailor claim that something had increased in it?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The excess is for the owner of the foodstuff, and the deficiency is upon him when there was a stipulation upon him for that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on excess and deficiency of goods in a hired ship contract according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'al-ghurm bi al-ghunm' (liability accompanies profit) in maritime logistics, clarifying that a carrier's liability for loss does not automatically extend to claiming ownership of surplus unless explicitly agreed. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on precise contractual stipulations, ensuring that the shipper retains the benefit of any unexpected gain while the carrier bears the risk of deficiency, reflecting the broader legal maxim that risk and reward must be balanced in commercial agreements.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, form Musa Bin Bakr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who hired a ship from a sailor, so he loaded it with foodstuff, and he stipulated upon him that if the foodstuff was deficient so it would be upon him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is allowed’. I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Sometimes the foodstuff is excessive’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Does the sailor claim that something had increased in it?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is for the owner of the foodstuff, the excess, and upon him would be the deficiency when there was a stipulation upon him for that’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who hired a ship from a sailor and loaded it with foodstuff, with the condition that if it was reduced he was liable. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible.’ I then said, ‘Perhaps it increases.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘Does the sailor claim that he has increased anything to it?’ I replied, ‘No, he does not claim.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It belongs to the owner of the foodstuff and he is liable for reduction if it is stipulated.’”
